correctness.rationale: For every extraspecial p-group, G/Z(G) is a nondegenerate symplectic F_p-space and commutation is exactly orthogonality. In dimension two each nonzero vector has orthogonal complement equal to its own line, yielding p+1 disjoint noncentral cliques of size p(p-1). In dimension at least four, the five displayed vectors have zero pairings exactly on the five cyclically consecutive pairs and nonzero pairings on the other five pairs; this remains true in characteristic two. Their representatives therefore induce C5, which is a forbidden induced subgraph for perfect graphs. The packaged checker independently verifies both mechanisms over p=2,3,5,7.

originality.rationale: The 2021 survey poses perfect commuting graphs as an open classification direction. The 2022 extraspecial recognition paper supplies the symplectic model and the order-p^3 clique structure but does not state a perfectness classification. Britnell--Gill classify quasisimple groups and give component restrictions, which do not classify component-free extraspecial p-groups. The 2023 forbidden-subgraph paper treats cograph, chordal, split, and threshold properties and restates the perfectness question without giving the extraspecial boundary. Targeted semantic and exact-phrase searches found no published statement of the all-rank extraspecial perfectness criterion or the uniform five-vector obstruction.
residual_risks: An equivalent higher-rank result may appear in finite-geometry literature on symplectic orthogonality graphs without using commuting-graph terminology.
The rank-one positive case is already compatible with prior CA-group and order-p^3 results; originality rests on the sharp extraspecial family boundary and uniform higher-rank C5.
Failed searches do not prove novelty.

value.rationale: Extraspecial p-groups are a standard and structurally central class of finite class-two groups, and their commuting graphs are explicitly highlighted in the recognition literature. The theorem gives a complete perfectness classification for the entire family, for all primes and both isomorphism types, with the boundary occurring at the first symplectic rank jump. The obstruction is a reusable five-vector configuration inside any two hyperbolic planes, making the result structural rather than a finite census.
